subject: Dedicated capacity — Performance acceptance criteria & pricing structure
messages:
From: Jessica Park <jessica.park@edgeai.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: EdgeAI Ops <ops@edgeai.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial sizing and cost question

Stephanie — thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're excited about Redwood Dedicated but want to pin down how performance commitments will map to pricing. Quick summary of our needs:
- Steady-state concurrent workload: ~400 qps at median request size ~120 tokens (prompt+gen)
- Spiky bursts up to 1.2k qps for short periods (1–3 min)
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile end-to-end < 300ms for 128-token generations; tail sensitivity above that
- Model family: Llama2-70B (quantized) and a smaller 13B for routing.

Two asks from our procurement team before we can sign: (1) a clear throughput/latency guarantee (tokens/sec and requests/sec) for the committed pool, and (2) an acceptance test definition and measurement method that we can run during the contract review window.

Can you provide a proposal that ties a reserved commit (GPU pool size) to guaranteed tokens/sec and a defined test harness? Also tell us how burst capacity and automatic fallback affect credits/SLAs.

Thanks — Jess
Jessica Park
Head of Platform, EdgeAI Inc.
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica.park@edgeai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial sizing and cost question

Jessica — great summary, and totally reasonable asks. High level answers below; I'll attach a short acceptance spec and sample workload file after this message. Follow-up: can we set up a 30m alignment session on Monday to walk the acceptance steps?

1) Pricing tiers + pool sizing (high level)
- Tier A (Committed 4x A100-equivalent GPUs): baseline sustained throughput target ~920k tokens/sec across the pool (~230k tps/GPU for quantized 70B under our benchmark); estimated median request-level throughput ~350–420 rps depending on batching.
- Tier B (Committed 8x GPUs): baseline ~1.9M tokens/sec; request-level throughput scales near-linearly for the same workload mix.
- Burst policy: 20% burst capacity is available for short windows (up to 5 min) without breaking the commit but does not increase SLA credits; larger bursts can be served from elastic capacity at a higher per-minute rate.

2) Guarantees & metrics framed for contract language
- Tokens/sec guarantee: Redwood guarantees the committed pool will sustain the advertised tokens/sec for the specified model family and quantization setting, measured as a 15-minute rolling average during business hours (M–F, 7am–7pm PT).
- Request/sec expectation: we provide a modeled rps per gpu figure based on your request-size distribution; contracts will include a conversion table (tokens->rps) that both sides sign off on.
- Latency SLOs: P50/P95 for a 128-token generation for the committed pool must meet the agreed numbers in the contract (example P95 <= 300ms). P99 and tail behavior are logged and monitored but not part of automatic crediting unless P99 exceeds a secondary threshold.

3) Measurement & acceptance testing (short summary)
- Acceptance harness: run a standardized script (we'll provide) against the Dedicated endpoint that replays a provided sample of 10k requests (edge-case + median mixes) over 30m. We measure 15-min rolling tokens/sec, P95 latency, and error rate.
- Pass criteria: sustained >= 95% of the promised tokens/sec and P95 latency within the contracted threshold for at least two non-overlapping 15-minute windows during the run.

4) Credits & failure modes
- If committed throughput guarantee is missed (under 95% of promised tokens/sec over the measurement window) and the root cause is within Redwood's serving infrastructure, Redwood will issue service credits pro-rated to the shortfall for that billing period.
- If miss is due to customer workload changes (unapproved model, larger prompt sizes, or different quantization), we'll flag as out-of-scope and propose remediation steps.

I'll attach the acceptance spec (PDF) and the sample workload JSONL. Aditya and Monica are copied for pricing delta and onboarding implications.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jessica Park <jessica.park@edgeai.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial sizing and cost question

Looping in pricing specifics so Jessica has concrete numbers for procurement. Jessica — below is a starter pricing construct we can formalize in the LOI: 

- Tier A (4x A100-eq reserved): $45k/month committed (blended), includes 20% burst pool at no extra charge up to 5 minutes per incident.
- Tier B (8x): $85k/month committed.
- Dedicated onboarding fee: one-time $12k (includes acceptance-run support and tuning).
- Volume discount: we can offer a 10% discount on committed MSRP for a 12-month prepay; 15% for 24-month prepay.

Pricing caveats: guarantees are tied to the model/quant settings in Attachment A (our acceptance spec). If EdgeAI wants different model compiling (custom kernels), we may need an engineering scope and a one-time integration fee.

Aditya
Aditya Rao
Director, Pricing & Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
From: Jessica Park <jessica.park@edgeai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: EdgeAI Ops <ops@edgeai.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 08:55:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial sizing and cost question

Thanks — clear and helpful. A few clarifying questions from our procurement and SRE teams: 
1) Measurement windows: are the business-hours constraints negotiable? Our traffic is global; we need an option for 24/7 measurement windows.
2) Acceptance run: we want the ability to run the acceptance harness from our CI (we'll provide runner hosts). Can Redwood provide a signed artifact (hash) of the acceptance script so we can validate the results independently?
3) SLA credits: can you share the formula you'd use for pro-rating credits (example: shortfall percent * committed monthly fee * adjustment factor)?

Also — the price looks reasonable if we can get 24/7 coverage and a 12-month prepay at 10% off. Would you be open to a 14-day signature window to lock these terms?

Jess
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jessica Park <jessica.park@edgeai.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Dec 2026 16:44:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial sizing and cost question

Jessica — quick follow-up addressing your three bullets and confirming next steps.

1) Measurement windows: we can offer two contract variants — Business Hours (M–F, 7am–7pm PT) or 24/7. The 24/7 variant increases the committed price by ~12% to account for nighttime staffing and cross-region capacity alignment. We'll mark both on the LOI so you can choose.

2) Acceptance harness integrity: yes — Redwood will provide the test script (open-source runner) and a signed SHA256 hash of the exact version we expect you to run. We'll also provide guidance for running from CI and an option for Redwood to run the script remotely while you stream logs for verification.

3) Credit formula (example implementation): ServiceCredit = min(CommittedFee, ShortfallPercent * CommittedFee * 0.9). ShortfallPercent = max(0, 1 - (MeasuredTokensSec / PromisedTokensSec)). We use a 0.9 adjustment factor to reflect partial mitigation from caching and transient burst absorption; this is negotiable for enterprise deals.

Next steps: we'll attach a draft LOI with both measurement-window options, the formal acceptance spec (PDF), and sample workload files. Proposal: 14-day signature window is acceptable. 

I'll attach the spec and workload now; planning 30m sync early next week to run through the acceptance steps and sign-off owners.

— Monica
Monica Patel
Sr. Manager, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
